newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Taiwan leaders warn of China impact on Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan leaders warn of China impact on Hong Kong.

text.p: Taiwan leaders warned in interviews published in Hong Kong on Thursday that the territory would feel the impact of authoritarian-style rule after Britain hands it back to China in mid-1997.
"Hong Kong's economic system may remain unchanged but politically Hong Kong is headed for retrenchment," Vice-President Lien Chan told the English-language Hong Kong Standard.
The paper also interviewed Foreign Minister John Chang, who said China would "commit the greatest blunder of the century" if it felt it had the right to stifle dissent in Hong Kong.
Chang was also sharply critical of China's decision to scrap Hong Kong's elected legislature, to limit press freedom and to deploy People's Liberation Army troops in the territory.
Beijing, which regains sovereignty over the territory at midnight next June 30, has promised Hong Kong a "high degree of autonomy" and no change to its capitalist system for 50 years.
But under mainland rule, political life in the capitalist territory of 6.2 million people would "bear the stamp of Peking's autocratic style", Lien said.
The interviews were also published in the daily's Chinese-language sister newspaper, the Sing Tao Daily.

"A so-called Hong Kong governed by the people of Hong Kong and the promised high degree of autonomy will only exist within the confines of the mainland's strict political framework," Lien said. He warned of far greater implications for Asia as a whole if China failed to keep its promise on Hong Kong's autonomy.
A breach of promise would impede economic reforms on the mainland and lead to political instability, which in turn would further affect regional development and security, Lien said.
China has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since the Chinese Nationalists took refuge there after losing a civil war to the Communists on the mainland in 1949.
On Wednesday Taiwan said it might be forced to shut down its representative offices in Hong Hong if China interfered with its operations after the handover.
